=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel: Buyer-side review of Seller update and Disclosure Letter

**Preliminary points**
- The Seller says these positions were "settled at principal level" and are FINAL. That is an unverified assertion in the Seller's own cover material. Please confirm with Wattlebridge principals what, if anything, was agreed before treating any term as closed.
- The "market" ranges (10-20% cap, ~1% basket, 12-18 months) are also the Seller's characterisation. They should be tested against our own precedents and not accepted as a benchmark.
- The Seller's own Disclosure Letter (paras 2-6) admits that Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, Ironquay payment evidence and the incident assessment are all unresolved. That contradicts the cover note's framing that they are "addressed" or "not material".

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims.
- **Buyer should want:** A higher cap (open at ~30%, AUD 7.2m), with fundamental, tax, fraud and specific indemnities outside it.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 30%, and accept 20% only if the carve-outs in 004, 005, 011, 012 and 014 are won. Reason: customer concentration (Bluefen ~30%) and open items make 20% thin, and the cap is acceptable only if it covers general warranties alone.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- **Seller:** AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 deductible basket (~1.04% of price), with only the excess recoverable.
- **Buyer should want:** A lower de minimis (~AUD 10,000), a tipping (first-dollar) basket at ~0.5% (~AUD 120,000), aggregation of related claims, and no thresholds for fundamental, tax, fraud or indemnity claims.
- **Recommendation:** Counter as above. Reason: a deductible basket at ~1% leaves the Buyer absorbing the first AUD 250k of any loss.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months, plus a drafting rule that any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer should want:** At least 24 months (covering a full audit cycle), longer periods for tax and title, and the default reversed so that limits apply only to claims expressly named.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24 months and reject the "applies to all Claims" default. Reason: the default silently sweeps in title, tax, indemnity and fraud claims.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties are subject to the same cap and time limits "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer should want:** Fundamental warranties capped at the full price (or proceeds), with no thresholds, a long limitation period (6+ years), and no disclosure or knowledge qualification.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Reason: title is the core of what we are buying, and a 20% cap and 18-month limit would leave up to 80% of the price unprotected against a title defect.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** Silent, and "all Claims of any nature" is caught by the limitation, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses (9.3/12.8/20.5).
- **Buyer should want:** Express carve-out so no limit, exclusive-remedy or non-reliance clause restricts claims for fraud, dishonest concealment or wilful misconduct, including statutory misleading-conduct claims.
- **Recommendation:** Insert as a non-negotiable. Reason: as drafted, the Seller's package could be read to limit recovery even for fraud, and that is unacceptable.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** Disclosure of the entire data room and public registers against all warranties (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter 1.1-1.2).
- **Buyer should want:** Specific disclosure only, against identified warranties and in fair detail. General data-room disclosure should not qualify fundamental or tax warranties, or defeat indemnities and conditions.
- **Recommendation:** Reject general disclosure. Reason: it lets the Seller defeat warranty claims by pointing to any document in the room.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** No claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, including matters "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer should want:** No knowledge qualifier. Fall back to actual knowledge of named individuals, limited to matters fairly disclosed, and with no effect on indemnities, fundamentals or fraud.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the constructive-knowledge limb. Reason: combined with 006, it would bar claims for almost everything the Buyer's own diligence surfaced, which is exactly why those items need conditions and specific indemnities.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** "Reasonable endeavours", with the condition treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. The Disclosure Letter admits no final consent and no evidence that clause 11.3 conditions are met.
- **Buyer should want:** A hard condition precedent: unconditional consent (or one with conditions satisfied or acceptable to the Buyer), in agreed form, before Completion. The Buyer alone can waive, with a long-stop date and termination right, and no concessions to Bluefen without Buyer approval.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the deemed-satisfied formulation. Reason: Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m (~30%) of FY26 revenue, and a consent with unmet conditions does not protect that revenue.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** Release to be provided after Completion (~AUD 3.2m outstanding).
- **Buyer should want:** Payout at Completion out of proceeds under a payout letter (including interest and break costs), with discharge of all security delivered at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release. Reason: this is a debt-free deal, and leaving security and change-control exposure (cl 8.1) on the Company after we pay is unacceptable.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** DD-005 closing bonuses (AUD 420,000) are the Seller's matter and not in the funds flow.
- **Buyer should want:** Bonuses, plus payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs, treated as Seller transaction costs or debt-like items, deducted from the price or paid by the Seller, backed by a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Require inclusion in the funds flow, with on-costs quantified. Reason: the Company is contractually liable, so unless deducted the Buyer bears at least AUD 420k of Seller-side cost.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** The indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment and is "adequate".
- **Buyer should want:** A condition requiring evidence of cleared payment (AUD 180k shown open in DD-010) and an executed confirmatory assignment of the SOW3 Project Materials, plus a broad, uncapped indemnity for any Ironquay claim over the IP.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "adequate". Reason: under DD-004 cl 7.3 the IP transfer depends on payment, so the real risk is ownership of core code, not the AUD 180k.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- **Seller:** Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material.
- **Buyer should want:** A completed investigation and notifiable-data-breach assessment before Completion, plus a specific indemnity (outside the cap and thresholds) for notification costs, regulatory action and third-party claims. The Buyer should have a say in how the matter is handled.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the Seller's characterisation and require the indemnity and pre-Completion covenant. Reason: ~1,240 personal records went to an unintended recipient, and the Disclosure Letter itself says access, scope and notification are unresolved. Likely Privacy Act exposure should be checked, and the incident date matters for any 30-day assessment timing.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** AUD 330k (3 × AUD 110k) is ordinary-course operating cost.
- **Buyer should want:** Facts on whether each renewal is committed, terminable, prepaid or accrued, when it was entered, and why three equal related renewals exist. Plus interim-period consent rights over new commitments.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the characterisation yet. If committed and outside ordinary course, treat as a price adjustment or debt-like item. Reason: the Disclosure Letter (para 8) does not support "ordinary course".

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** One regime (cap, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedy, non-reliance) applies to every Claim.
- **Buyer should want:** Separate tiers: (1) general warranties (cap, thresholds, 18-24 months); (2) fundamental/title (price cap, long tail); (3) tax (own indemnity, long tail); (4) specific indemnities (Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, incident) with no cap or thresholds; (5) fraud, unlimited. Cl 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 should be limited to tier 1.
- **Recommendation:** Restructure along these lines. Reason: this is the structural fix that makes the numerical positions on cap and time acceptable.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the Company's own share register (DD-012). The Disclosure Letter says this is not Buyer verification.
- **Buyer should want:** Independent verification (ASIC extract, transfer history, constitution and shareholder arrangements, PPSR and encumbrance searches including any share security under Riverlark, options or pre-emption rights), plus Completion deliverables: executed transfers, share certificates and security releases.
- **Recommendation:** Complete the checks before signing and make deliverables a Completion condition. Reason: the register is the Seller's own record and proves little on its own.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- **Seller:** Settled under the general regime.
- **Buyer should want:** A standalone pre-Completion tax indemnity (outside the cap, with a long limitation period tied to the amendment period), and strengthened IP warranties (ownership, contractor and employee assignments, third-party and open-source claims) with a higher cap or fundamental treatment.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "settled" and keep these open. Reason: nothing in the record shows agreement, and the Ironquay issue shows IP ownership is a live risk.

---

**Suggested next steps**
1. Confirm with principals what was actually agreed (Seller's "FINAL" claim).
2. Prepare a mark-up implementing the tiered structure in 014.
3. Send diligence requests on Bluefen conditions, Ironquay payment evidence, incident timeline, Sandbar contracts, bonus on-costs, and title searches.
4. Re-run the funds flow with Riverlark payout and bonuses deducted.

I can draft the mark-up language or a request list next if useful.
